t: This is St Peter, Vere Street, a former Anglican church just off Oxford Street. Until 1832 it was known as the Oxford Chapel, after its founder Edward Harley, the 2nd Earl of Oxford. It has also been called the Marybone or Marylebone Chapel. The building was designed by James Gibbs, a Scottish architect born in Aberdeen and trained in Rome. His work spans the move from English Baroque to Georgian architecture, and his best-known buildings include St Martin-in-the-Fields and the Radcliffe Camera in Oxford.
